audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Isaac famine/sojourning, promise repetition, Rebekah sister-wife episode, wells/conflict, Rehoboth, Beersheba oath, and Esau's Hittite marriages.

verses.restored: There was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

familiar.text: And there was a famine in the land, beside the first famine...

notes.title: Isaac repeats Abraham patterns
notes.body: Famine, Gerar, Abimelech, and wife-as-sister motifs echo Abraham’s story.

modern.text: Now there was another famine in the land, subsequent to the one that had occurred in Abraham’s time. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יִצְחָ֛ק אֶל אֲבִימֶּ֥לֶךְ מֶֽלֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים גְּרָֽרָה

verses.restored: The Eternal appeared to him and said, Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land that I tell you.

familiar.text: And the LORD appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt...

modern.text: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land where I tell you.

original.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה שְׁכֹ֣ן בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your seed I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.

familiar.text: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee...

notes.title: Promise renewed to Isaac
notes.body: The Abrahamic promise is explicitly transferred to Isaac: presence, blessing, seed, land, and oath.

modern.text: Stay in this land as a foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring, and I will confirm the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.

original.text: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי לְךָ֣ וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֗ אֶתֵּן֙ אֶת כָּל הָֽאֲרָצֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ

verses.restored: I will multiply your seed like the stars of the heavens, and I will give to your seed all these lands. In your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,

familiar.text: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven...

modern.text: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed,

original.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֤י אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְזַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל הָאֲרָצֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑ל וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: because Abraham listened to my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my instructions.

familiar.text: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge...

modern.text: because Abraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.” Isaac Deceives Abimelech

original.text: עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָהָ֖ם בְּקֹלִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֔י מִצְוֺתַ֖י חֻקּוֹתַ֥י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי

verses.restored: So Isaac dwelled in Gerar.

familiar.text: And Isaac dwelt in Gerar:

modern.text: So Isaac settled in Gerar.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִצְחָ֖ק בִּגְרָֽר

verses.restored: The men of the place asked about his woman. He said, She is my sister, for he feared to say, My woman, lest the men of the place kill me because of Rebekah, for she was good in appearance.

familiar.text: And the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister...

notes.title: Sister-wife pattern again
notes.body: Isaac repeats the fear-driven deception seen with Abraham and Sarah.

modern.text: But when the men of that place asked about his wife, he said, “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” since he thought to himself, “The men of this place will kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is so beautiful.”

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽיא

verses.restored: When he had been there many days, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through the window and saw, and look, Isaac was laughing/caressing Rebekah his woman.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time... Isaac was sporting with Rebekah...

notes.title: Laughing/caressing
notes.body: Metsacheq is related to Isaac’s laughter-name and here shows marital intimacy, exposing the deception.

modern.text: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from the window and was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֣י אָֽרְכוּ ל֥וֹ שָׁם֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Abimelech called Isaac and said, Surely she is your woman. How then did you say, She is my sister? Isaac said to him, Because I said, Lest I die because of her.

familiar.text: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy wife...

modern.text: Abimelech sent for Isaac and said, “So she is really your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac replied, “Because I thought I might die on account of her.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Abimelech said, What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your woman, and you would have brought guilt upon us.

familiar.text: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us?...

notes.title: Guilt avoided
notes.body: As in Genesis 20, the foreign king recognizes the danger of covenant household deception.

modern.text: “What is this you have done to us?” asked Abimelech. “One of the people could easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ מַה זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ כִּ֠מְעַט שָׁכַ֞ב אַחַ֤ד הָעָם֙ אֶת אִשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ עָלֵ֖ינוּ אָשָֽׁם

verses.restored: Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, Whoever touches this man or his woman shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man...

modern.text: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever harms this man or his wife will surely be put to death.” Isaac’s Prosperity

original.text: וַיְצַ֣ו אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ אֶת כָּל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Eternal blessed him.

familiar.text: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold...

modern.text: Now Isaac sowed seed in the land, and that very year he reaped a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him,

original.text: וַיִּזְרַ֤ע יִצְחָק֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיִּמְצָ֛א בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַהִ֖וא מֵאָ֣ה שְׁעָרִ֑ים וַֽיְבָרֲכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: The man became great, and he kept going and becoming great until he became very great.

familiar.text: And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great:

modern.text: and he became richer and richer, until he was exceedingly wealthy.

original.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: He had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and many servants, and the Philistines envied him.

familiar.text: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds...

modern.text: He owned so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: All the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up and filled with dust.

familiar.text: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged...

modern.text: So the Philistines took dirt and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.

original.text: וְכָל הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו סִתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְמַלְא֖וּם עָפָֽר

verses.restored: Abimelech said to Isaac, Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we are.

familiar.text: And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than we.

modern.text: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Depart from us, for you are much too powerful for us.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל יִצְחָ֑ק לֵ֚ךְ מֵֽעִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי עָצַֽמְתָּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Isaac went from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelled there.

familiar.text: And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar...

modern.text: So Isaac left that place and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם יִצְחָ֑ק וַיִּ֥חַן בְּנַֽחַל גְּרָ֖ר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham’s death, and he called their names by the names his father had called them.

familiar.text: And Isaac digged again the wells of water...

notes.title: Re-digging wells
notes.body: Isaac restores Abraham’s wells and names, re-opening ancestral life sources.

modern.text: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died. And he gave these wells the same names his father had given them.

original.text: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר אֶת בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו וַיְסַתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found there a well of living water.

familiar.text: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.

notes.title: Living water
notes.body: Mayim chayyim means living/running water, not stagnant water.

modern.text: Then Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water there.

original.text: וַיַּחְפְּר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי יִצְחָ֖ק בַּנָּ֑חַל וַיִּ֨מְצְאוּ שָׁ֔ם בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֥יִם חַיִּֽים

verses.restored: The herders of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herders, saying, The water is ours. He called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

familiar.text: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen...

modern.text: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen and said, “The water is ours!” So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him.

original.text: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: They dug another well, and they quarreled over that also, so he called its name Sitnah.

familiar.text: And they digged another well, and strove for that also...

modern.text: Then they dug another well and quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.

original.text: וַֽיַּחְפְּרוּ֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיָּרִ֖יבוּ גַּם עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמָ֖הּ שִׂטְנָֽה

verses.restored: He moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He called its name Rehoboth and said, For now the Eternal has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.

familiar.text: And he removed from thence, and digged another well...

notes.title: Rehoboth
notes.body: Rehoboth comes from room/broad space. Conflict gives way to spaciousness.

modern.text: He moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He named it Rehoboth and said, “At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”

original.text: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: From there he went up to Beersheba.

familiar.text: And he went up from thence to Beersheba.

modern.text: From there Isaac went up to Beersheba,

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע

verses.restored: The Eternal appeared to him that night and said, I am the Divine of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham my servant.

familiar.text: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night...

modern.text: and that night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham.”

original.text: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ אַל תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֨יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי

verses.restored: He built an altar there and called on the name of the Eternal. He pitched his tent there, and Isaac’s servants dug a well there.

familiar.text: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD...

modern.text: So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and he pitched his tent there. His servants also dug a well there. Isaac’s Covenant with Abimelech

original.text: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וַיֶּט שָׁ֖ם אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּכְרוּ שָׁ֥ם עַבְדֵי יִצְחָ֖ק בְּאֵֽר

verses.restored: Abimelech came to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his companion and Phicol commander of his army.

familiar.text: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends...

modern.text: Later, Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.

original.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֕לֶךְ הָלַ֥ךְ אֵלָ֖יו מִגְּרָ֑ר וַאֲחֻזַּת֙ מֵֽרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּפִיכֹ֖ל שַׂר צְבָאֽוֹ

verses.restored: Isaac said to them, Why have you come to me, since you hated me and sent me away from you?

familiar.text: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me...

modern.text: “Why have you come to me?” Isaac asked them. “You hated me and sent me away.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י וְאַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וַתְּשַׁלְּח֖וּנִי מֵאִתְּכֶֽם

verses.restored: They said, We have clearly seen that the Eternal has been with you, and we said, Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us cut a covenant with you,

familiar.text: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee...

modern.text: “We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you,” they replied. “We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ רָא֣וֹ רָאִינוּ֮ כִּֽי הָיָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּךְ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you, and just as we have done to you only good and sent you away in peace. You are now blessed of the Eternal.

familiar.text: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee...

modern.text: that you will not harm us, just as we have not harmed you but have done only good to you, sending you on your way in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD.”

original.text: אִם תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם אַתָּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה בְּר֥וּךְ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: He made them a feast, and they ate and drank.

familiar.text: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.

modern.text: So Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ

verses.restored: They rose early in the morning and swore to one another. Isaac sent them away, and they went from him in peace.

familiar.text: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another...

modern.text: And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְאָחִ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֣ם יִצְחָ֔ק וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: That same day Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, We have found water.

familiar.text: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came...

modern.text: On that same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. “We have found water!” they told him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ מָצָ֥אנוּ מָֽיִם

verses.restored: He called it Shibah. Therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.

familiar.text: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city is Beersheba...

notes.title: Shibah / Beersheba
notes.body: The name plays again on oath/seven and well.

modern.text: So he called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the city is Beersheba. Esau’s Wives

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁבְעָ֑ה עַל כֵּ֤ן שֵׁם הָעִיר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: When Esau was forty years old, he took Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite as women.

familiar.text: And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith...

modern.text: When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ בֶּן אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת יְהוּדִ֔ית בַּת בְּאֵרִ֖י הַֽחִתִּ֑י וְאֶת בָּ֣שְׂמַ֔ת בַּת אֵילֹ֖ן הַֽחִתִּֽי

verses.restored: They were bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.

familiar.text: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.

notes.title: Bitterness of spirit
notes.body: The phrase names deep distress caused by Esau’s marriages.

modern.text: And they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

original.text: וַתִּהְיֶ֖יןָ מֹ֣רַת ר֑וּחַ לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּלְרִבְקָֽה
